findings.where: Section 6, word-list row 693 ("the premise the underdetermination proof carries")
findings.claim_in_model: "Where a family's relations are computed from one parameter set, the proof's second limb applies and the population, not the history, fixes the untested value."

A parametric family generally does contain many members that agree on H and differ off it, so the antecedent is not discharged by parameterisation. findings.where: Part B3 (W7 lines 248, 256) and word-list row 727
findings.claim_in_model: B3: "if the carrier carries everything the process carried, no admitted change on the contract separates them, and they are one account at that grain." Two arrangements of one reader are not candidates in that sense, and agreeing on a field is not satisfying the three conditions. What the arms' agreement is held by is the Consequence alone, which B3 also quotes and which says only that the contract does not contain the distinction. Row 727 as written also pulls against row 698, which forbids exactly this read ("never as a claim that two arrangements are one organization, which Part 0 forbids"), and section 4 does not record the pull.

A candidate is defined at file 11 line 233: "An explanatory candidate for question \(p\) is an organization \(E\), a transport \(t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\) from \(D\) to \(E\), and an identified set \(\Gamma\) of active commitments in \(E\)." The Consequence, line 558, which is what B3 quotes as its holder: "Underdetermination of an account by a contract is not a failure of the semantics to decide; it is the semantics reporting that the contract does not contain the distinction." verdict:
1. THE QUESTION, FROZEN. What is being explained: whether W7's use of Semantics file 11 holds — whether every quotation W7 gives as file 11's is verbatim in file 11 at the Part named, with the right two-file mark; whether each word-list row is read no wider than the sentence it quotes (W3 section 7 as W5 section 1 rewords it: holds | loose, with the nearer passage named | construction, marked or not | contradicts, with the sentence quoted); whether every construction is marked with its permitting passages; whether the eleven H69 notions each get a row or a reason; and whether the sentence of file 11 that a part names as its holder holds that part as the builder says. Over what range: the whole of W7 — 34 parts, 75 word-list rows plus 4 added by the assembly, 21 table rows with their holders, and the eleven notions. What is asked: a rule-status question (does this count as a faithful use of the authority under the plan's own rule), not a production question about agents. Held still throughout; nothing in file 11 or file 10 was written to, and no shell command was run.

2. THE EXPLANATION IN PARTS, AND THE JOBS. The parts under my remit are the quotations, the marks and the rows, not the model's account of agents. The jobs are the plan's, all given: W6.1 (every row quotes file 11 with Part and file mark, zero contradicting, zero unmarked constructions), W6.3 (the eleven notions, with the fourth and eighth as rows), and the standing rule from W5 section 1 that the mark exists so that what rests on file 11 alone can be found if round S76 does not let file 11 stand. I added no job. The correction I was told to carry — that "fitted" maps to Derivation 3 in its qualified form only — I applied to every mark; W7 carries the qualification correctly in the parts (A5, B6) and in rows 692 and 726, which name the unqualified form and forbid it. It drops the qualification once, in row 693, and drops it toward the population rather than toward the history.

3. PART BY PART. Thirty-four parts, each with a quoted holder, a provenance, a mark and a falsifier. On the file-11 side the work is good: I checked every rests-on quotation and every holder against file 11 line by line, and every one is verbatim at the Part named. The two-file marks are right in 79 of 81 places I checked. The two that are wrong are opposite errors and both come from the builders' returns unchanged: A6's Part XII sentence is marked "11 only" and is verbatim in file 10 line 482; B9's Part VIII recoding sentence is marked "10 and 11" and file 10 has no Recoding paragraph at all. Both are forced edits, and both matter for exactly the reason W5 built the mark. My marks agree with the builders' on 31 of 34 parts. They part company on three. A7's second clause — "Where two arms emit differently under the same inputs, they are different organizations at this grain" — is held by neither of its quoted sentences and is said otherwise by Part II's "Several solutions remain several" read with (O); the model's own A3 draws that conclusion from that sentence, so the contradiction is internal as well as against file 11. B3's "they are one account at that grain" needs Derivation 2's Claim, whose antecedent is two explanatory candidates for one question each satisfying (F1), (F2) and (A), which two arrangements of one reader do not meet; B3's own falsifier names the gap, so the part is held if that reading stands. C11's rule is held by a swap that fails, but the reason it gives for its first rider — "a system cannot declare those of itself without the circularity the theory forbids" — is nowhere in file 11, and Part XIV's declared-inputs paragraph puts the contract's scope on the same side as the boundary and continuity, so the line the rider draws is not the theory's; three of the four examples in its second failing swap are held in the record column by their need of a history, not by an index. Of the rows: one contradicts (697), six or seven are loose (688, 691, 693, 704, 708, 727, 752), eleven are marked constructions and all eleven name their permitting passages, and nothing else marked "holds" is a construction on a forced reading. All constructions in the parts are marked as such (A1, A2, A4, A5, A8, B2, B5, C11, C12) with the passages named.

4. WHOLE-EXPLANATION CHECKS, by their Step 5 names. REMOVE bit: remove Part II's "Several solutions remain several" and A3 falls outright; remove Part X's port sentence and A2's port limb and A4's placement of the injected passages both fall; remove Part XIV's declared-inputs paragraph and B1 falls. SWAP bit hardest: swap each row's quotation for the nearest passage at the same Part and four rows change meaning (688, 693, 704, 708 and 752) while the other seventy do not — which is the honest report that the list is tight in seventy places and loose in four or five, and that its looseness is concentrated where a row's gloss reaches past its sentence. POKE bit: change a file mark and watch whether anything in W7 moves — nothing does, because no rig in this round checks against file 10; that is the "would move" half failing and it is what let the two wrong marks through. The "would not move" half, next to the line: change a quotation's whitespace and nothing moves, correctly. PULL bit: rows 698 and 727 pull against each other on Derivation 2, and A3 pulls against A7 on Part II; section 4 records neither, though it records twelve other seams. HUNT THE ANSWER IN THE STARTING POINTS bit, and it is where builder C asked a judge to press first: C11's first rider is where the wanted answer could be sitting, and the rider's stated reason is not on file 11's words, though the rule survives on the Can swap. ADD A JOB bit: require every quotation to be checked against file 10 as well as file 11, and two rests-on fail at once; that job rules out the version of W7 in which the marks were never checked, and it is the cheapest job available. CHECK THE PATCHES bit: C10's note on its own file mark is a patch that records what it gives up, which is the right habit; the assembly's merge rule at line 675 is the opposite — a claim that the rows were merged one per term, which at least five terms falsify silently. FLIP THE OUTCOME could not bite: a quotation is verbatim or it is not, and there is no opposite outcome to have been explained just as well; the sentence that leaves it nothing to reach is section 6's "Every row quotes file 11 at the Part named with its file mark." REVERSE could not bite: the direction between a row and the sentence it quotes is fixed by the quotation, and neither end can be poked from here — file 11 is read-only and this round writes nothing. BUILD THE BEST RIVAL did bite, and the rival is the one named under SWAP: a word list that quotes the nearest passage for every row. It differs from W7's on four or five rows and nowhere else, so at this level the two are the same list except there; that is the finer question the four rows record. LOOK INSIDE could not bite on my question: the workings a quotation check reaches are the text of file 11 and nothing behind it; W7 names the same limit in its own place (A10: "look inside ... cannot bite on a single document"). The part it would have settled — whether the builders read file 11 or matched its shape — is left unknown, with that test named.

5. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT HARDER TO VARY. First: run the W5 quote-check program over W7 against file 10 as well as file 11 and set every mark from the pair. It is a program that already exists, it would have caught both wrong marks, and until it runs the file marks are unknown as a class rather than wrong in two places. Second: make every row quote the nearest passage that says what the row says, which is four or five edits and turns the loosest rows in the list into held ones.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. That W7 is right about LLM agents. That file 11 is right about anything: file 11 is itself under test in round S76, and every "11 only" mark in W7 marks something that would have to be re-derived if it does not stand — which is why the two wrong marks matter more than their size. That the parts are good explanations under the skill's full procedure: that is the procedure judge's, and my marks on A7, B3 and C11 should be read beside that judge's before any of the three is changed. Nothing here is a test of the model; every quotation I checked was already in the record before I read it.
